statement: Let d0 be the threshold in Theorem 1.1. For every admissible d > d0, a very general X ∈ Cd is irrational and admits a labelling K of discriminant d and a primitively polarized smooth projective K3 surface (SHdg, L), with L2 = d, for which there is an integral Hodge isometry K⊥ ≃ L⊥ (−1). Here L⊥ ⊂ H2(SHdg, Z), and the surface cup pairing is reversed. Thus an associated untwisted polarized K3 surface in this Hodge-theoretic sense is not sufficient for rationality.
